newsitem.title: USA: OUTLOOK - Larger US crop output in '97, income dips.
newsitem.headline: OUTLOOK - Larger US crop output in '97, income dips.

text.p: U.S. farmers will exercise the new "Freedom to Farm" law to grow more corn, wheat and soybeans this year while cutting back on cotton and rice, the Agriculture Department estimated Monday.

As a result, USDA said in a report released at its annual Outlook Forum, U.S. grain and soybean exports would boom and cotton would remain strong. Ending stocks would climb modestly for major U.S. crops except cotton, where strong global demand would cut into the domestic stockpile.
The report assumed normal conditions and yields. USDA will not make formal forecasts until harvest is ready.

In the long run, USDA said, "a tightening of the balance between productive capacity and projected demands results in rising nominal market prices, increasing farm income and stability in the financial condition of the (farm) sector."

Net farm income was forecast to drop to $40.4 billion this year, compared to $51.8 billion last year, but strengthen after 1998. Much of the decline was due to the drop-off in grain prices from the heady levels of the past two years.
Ag exports were projected for $55.5 billion in fiscal 1997, down from the record $59.8 billion of fiscal 1996.
